The paradox

Born
Got a middle-class life.
Built everything
anyway.

Both halves are true, and neither explains the other. The money story and the life story do not match. What came out of the mismatch is this: a lab with no safety-net cosplay and no trust-fund shortcuts, building like rent is due, because functionally it is.

Bootstrapped, all of it. Nivelato Labs: founded 2026, $0 raised, no investors, no board, team of one human. Every product on this page was built the unglamorous way, out of a family glass shop's actual problems, on hardware already in the room.

AI-first fuckery, since day one. On AI since ChatGPT came out, not since it got fashionable. The lab runs AI-first to a degree that stops being a workflow and becomes a philosophy: a grid of agents designing, building, researching and reviewing, a thesis written by AI and defended by a human, benchmarks for agents doing fully autonomous work. One human at the top, a fleet underneath, shipping like a company ten times its size.

Nivelato Labs — the catalog

Built like an empire.
Priced like a neighbor.

Nivelato

Flagship — glass shop operations

Measurement to quote to job to invoice, for glass shops. Born on a real shop floor in San Juan, built for the small shops enterprise software forgot. Every feature free until the Android app publishes on Google Play. iOS, in Liquid Glass, is coming.

nivelatolabs.com

Attune

Research — agent harness

One harness, two model series. Long-horizon autonomous work, measured in hours, not demos. The lab's bet that a model behind the frontier, trained on real long tasks, outworks a bigger model on short ones.

nivelatolabs.com/attune

PhoneBench

Open benchmark — Apache-2.0

A first-of-its-kind benchmark for fully autonomous work: an agent, a phone, a real task, no hand-holding. Public, open source, run it yourself.

nivelatolabs.com

Product — a vending machine front end

Snacks, dispensed. A touch-first vending front end with its own mark and one small-print byline: a Nivelato Labs product.

Advocacy

Autism is not
a defect.
It is a difference.

The advocacy is not a side project, it is the same project. Software for the shops the industry skipped, research for the people the paradigm skipped, published where anyone can read it, priced so the smallest operation in the room can use it.

The Thesis

Neurodiversity paradigm — open preprint

A full-length argument against the cure narrative and for the neurodiversity paradigm, built with AI, reviewed by humans, published open on OSF. UCL autism researcher William Mandy called it "a very convincing case for the neurodiversity paradigm."

Read it on OSF

Access, as policy

Free flagship — open benchmark — open research

Advocacy you can measure: Nivelato's features are free while it launches, PhoneBench is open source under Apache-2.0, and the research is a public preprint, not a paywalled PDF. If the work helps, it ships where people can reach it.

nivelatolabs.com

In the room

Accommodations — inclusion — service

In direct contact with families working out neurodiversity accommodations, in a church community rated 9.9 out of 10 for neurodiversity inclusion from the inside, and in volunteer emergency-response and cadet-program service in Puerto Rico. Advocacy that shows up in person, not just in posts.

The community record

The stance

Anti-cure — pro-difference

Neurological diversity is not a problem to be corrected. It is a reality to build for. Every product decision on this page, who gets access, who gets accommodated, who gets believed, runs on that sentence.

Why it is personal

Core proficiency — efficient AI use

AI is not a feature.
It is the staff.

Extremely good at this, and able to prove it. On AI since ChatGPT launched in 2022. First coding agent June 2026, self-measured at roughly a 70x productivity jump. The skill is not prompting, it is operations: fleets of agents run like a company, with coordinators, gates, budgets and verification, while one human keeps the judgment.

Orchestration

Multi-agent systems

Designs and runs agent fleets: single coordinators, parallel swarms, wave discipline with pass/fail gates, red-team critique rounds, and morning-after digests instead of babysitting runs.

Verification

Nothing ships on vibes

Every agent claim gets checked against primary sources. Citation audits (276 citations checked on one paper), formal proof loops in Lean 4, and critic swarms whose findings are themselves verified before anything is rewritten.

Token economics

Efficiency is the whole game

Burn-rate monitoring, model routing (a small always-on router, the big model only when the task earns it), quantization discipline on local models, and budgets treated like money, because they are.

Local inference

Own hardware, own models

Runs her own models on her own machines: a 9B everyday model and a 27B big slot, skills and memory installed into local hosts, zero cloud dependency for the private work.

Evaluation

Benchmarks, not impressions

Builds the tests instead of trusting the demos: PhoneBench for fully autonomous phone work, fixed probe gauntlets with scoring rubrics for small models, graded-duration measurement for long-horizon claims.

The record

Output, counted

A 33-page exegesis from a 30-agent swarm with 5 peer-review cycles. A 46-page research report from 16,407 items pulled and 2,307 coded. Training-trace campaigns run in gated waves of hundreds of thousands of tokens. That is what efficient looks like.

Why it exists

Imposing,
on purpose.
Helpful,
on the record.

Nivelato started with one quoting desk in one family glass shop in Puerto Rico, where quotes took hours of unpaid work. The fix was not a bigger company. It was software a small shop could actually run. So the flagship is free while it launches, the benchmark is open source, the research is published where anyone can read it, and the smallest shops get the same system as the biggest. Rich and autistic is not a flex. It is a proof of concept: the kid the system did not build for, building for everyone it skipped.
